heading: Level benefit or graded benefit, in 74 seconds
name: Final expense: level benefit or graded benefit?
description: A level (immediate) benefit can pay the full benefit from day 1 if your health qualifies. A graded benefit has a waiting period, often the first 2 or 3 years; here is how each one works and 3 questions to ask before you apply.
transcript: Final expense: level benefit or graded benefit? Here is how each one works. A level benefit is also called an immediate benefit. If your health qualifies, it can pay the full benefit from day 1. A graded benefit has a waiting period, often the first 2 or 3 years. If death is from natural causes in that time, the beneficiary receives a reduced amount. Often that is the premiums paid, with some interest, or a percentage of the benefit. After that period, the full face amount is paid. Level: the full benefit from day 1. Graded: a reduced amount early, then the full benefit. Many policies pay accidental death in full from day 1. Your health answers decide which one is offered. Some health conditions rule out a level benefit. Policies with no health questions are typically graded. Some answers place you in a graded class. Before you apply, ask 3 questions. How long is the grading period? What does my beneficiary receive in that time? Does accidental death pay in full? Want to talk it through?
